mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last month signals labor market weakness, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over the last two quarters signals a weakening economy, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and investor confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the periods following a sustained GDP decline, or if the correlation between GDP declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in the last month signals a strong supply-side response, which leads to increased productivity and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increases on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and potential wage inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of low UNRATE and high PAYEMS increases on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in the last two months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which leads to reduced economic activity and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between HOUST decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is positive and industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 1% in the last month, it signals a strong economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 0% and INDPRO increases > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of positive GDPC1 growth and INDPRO increases on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
